title: W1 negative test covers only header/parse drift classes — hash-level (payload) drift rejection is never exercised as a negative test
evidence: make_drift_mutations: 'append(&out, mutated(src, "catalog_hash", proc(b: []u8) { b[17] ~= 0xFF }))' / 'append(&out, mutated(src, "logic_hz", proc(b: []u8) { b[25] ~= 0x01 }))' / 'append(&out, mutated(src, "bad_magic", proc(b: []u8) { b[0] ~= 0xFF }))' / 'append(&out, mutated(src, "bad_version", proc(b: []u8) { b[4] = 99 }))' / 'append(&out, mutated(src, "bad_tag", proc(b: []u8) { b[41] = 0xFF }))' / '// truncation — drop the last byte.' Oracle: '_, accepted := replay_hashes(tmp, cat, ticks, &fails)' then 'if accepted { ... fmt.eprintfln("drift-check: %s: FAIL — gate ACCEPTED drifted log (%s)", name, m.label); bad += 1 }' — replay_hashes performs no manifest/hash comparison; the only hash comparison lives in verify_replay (positive path, harness run). Header comment: '// unknown command tag (byte 41 = header 33 + apply_tick 8).' — command payloads start at byte 42 and no mutation touches bytes 33..40 (apply_tick) or 42..51 (a/b/tier).
detail: All six mutation classes are parse/header-level (rejected before hashing). A payload drift that stays parseable (e.g. an apply_tick or tier flip) re-sims cleanly and is treated as 'accepted', so the hash-divergence rejection — replay-equality's load-bearing protection — is never proven negatively in CI.
recommended_fix: Add a payload-drift mutation (flip an apply_tick or tier byte) and assert the re-sim's hashes DIVERGE from the blessed manifest (hash-compare oracle), not merely that replay_hashes refuses to parse.

title: Self-loop drag is filtered before validation: the .Self_Loop rejection never surfaces in the app UI
evidence: 'if id, ok := snap_node(app, wx, wy); ok && id != app.drag.from_node {' ... '} else { app.drag_to = 0; app.drag.valid = .None; app.drag.cost = 0 }' ... 'if rl.IsMouseButtonReleased(.LEFT) { // commit if snapped to a legal target if app.drag_to != 0 && app.drag.valid == .None {' — releasing on the drag's own node takes the else branch, so a Cmd_Draw_Pipe with a == b is never built. reject_label (app/main.odin:204): 'case .Self_Loop: return "can't draw a pipe from a node to itself"' is unreachable from this path. Core pins the typed error: core/topology_test.odin:28 'testing.expect(t, err == .Self_Loop, "node→itself must reject with .Self_Loop (E3)")'.
detail: Story card AC: 'a self-loop drag (node→itself) is rejected with .Self_Loop [E3]'. Core + test satisfy the typed contract and no pipe is created, but the app silently no-ops (ghost stays green) — the player never sees the E3 rejection feedback.
recommended_fix: On release over the drag's own node, run validate_draw on {from_node, from_node} (or set drag.valid = .Self_Loop) so the typed rejection and hint reach the player instead of a silent no-op.

title: draw_building carried near-verbatim from the reference prototype — partial from-scratch compliance
evidence: draw_building body (v2) is byte-identical to prototype-ref app/render/view.odin draw_building apart from the signature — same magic constants: 'w := s * 1.15' / 'h := s * 0.95' / 'rl.DrawRectangleV({c.x - w/2, c.y - h/2 + s*0.12}, {w, h - s*0.12}, p.host_body)' / 'rl.DrawRectangleV({c.x - w/2, c.y - h/2}, {w, s * 0.28}, p.host_roof)' / 'rl.DrawTriangle(v3, v2, v1, {250, 246, 238, 255})' / 'variant := int(id) % 4' / 'w := s * 0.92' / 'h := s * 0.62' / 'top := c.y - h * 0.15' / 'dw := s * 0.16' / 'rl.DrawRectangleV({c.x - dw/2, top + h - s * 0.3}, {dw, s * 0.3}, roof)' (27/35 lines identical; tier_pipe_color/tier_pipe_width switches 7/9 identical). Job briefing mandate: 'Fresh code on v2 — prototype is reference-only … rebuild clean'.
detail: The world pass and topology are genuinely rebuilt (draw_pipes/draw_ghost/draw_router 13-28% overlap; topology.odin drops the prototype's maps and half its fields), so this is not a wholesale copy — but one leaf render proc plus two switches were carried verbatim, a soft-spot on the from-scratch mandate.
recommended_fix: Re-author draw_building with distinct geometry/constants (and the two tier switches), or explicitly note the sanctioned design-mining reuse in the PR body.

title: catalog.odin comment promises unknown JSON fields abort; the loader silently ignores them
evidence: Comment: 'loaded once, fail-fast validated (unknown fields, out-of-range values, missing required content abort with a named error)'. But data/node_types.json:10 ships '"lb_mode_capable": false' and Node_Type has no such field — catalogs_load reads only id/display_name/kind/terminal_role/throughput_units/port_capacity/era_introduced via jstr/jint, so the unknown key is silently skipped, no error returned.
detail: A misspelled/unknown JSON key silently defaults instead of aborting, contradicting the code's own stated ODN-5 contract. Currently harmless (raw bytes still ride in catalog_hash, so replay binding stays honest), but a typo'd field silently changes behavior.
recommended_fix: After parsing each entry, verify every key against the known set and return a named error on unknowns (matching the comment), or amend the comment to state unknown fields are ignored.
